summary: Plumas National Forest lookout on the Claremont summits south of Quincy, planned in 1907 and staffed by 1909; gone, with telecom towers on the summit now.

facts.status_note: The lookout is gone; the summit now holds telecom towers and equipment.

visit.trail_note: Dirt forest roads reach the summits, according to a trip report; no lookout remains to visit.

events.note: Newspaper: telephone line, ranger camp and lookout station planned for the summit
Completed June 1908, according to one trip report; the 1907 notices only planned it
Station maintained for the summer season; the newspaper names no staff
Forest officers extinguished or helped extinguish 85 fires that season; the station helped locate fires
Newspaper: Claremont and Mount Hough named as the two lookout peaks to be maintained
By the 1930s the lookout was no longer used; a 2022 trip report says no sign of it can be seen today
The 2020 Claremont Fire burned forest along the 2022 trip route; the trip report does not say it reached the summits (Adventure Taco)

corrections.why: The lookout page is headed Claremont Mountain; the record's name stops partway through the word.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three names appear: Claremont Mountain (lookout page), Claremont Peak (2022 trip report) and Claremont (firelookout.org list). The story uses Claremont Mountain for the lookout site.
The 1907 notices planned a lookout for the 1908 season; only one trip report gives the June 1908 completion date.

notes_for_editor: Single-source points: the June 1908 completion and the 'by the 1930s' abandonment both come from one blog post (Adventure Taco); the story gives the 1930s only as a decade. Record point (39.8836, -120.945) is about 1.2 km from the firelookout.org point (39.88529, -120.93106), so no coordinate correction is proposed. No source says whether the summits are open to the public. The telecom towers are not a lookout and are not suggested for climbing. Staffing 'staffed' for 1909 rests on the maintenance notices; no staff are named. The 2020 fire is sourced only for the 2022 trip route; the summits are not confirmed as burned.
